assessment.title: B2 Level Assessment
assessment.description: A comprehensive assessment of B2 grammar, vocabulary, reading, listening, and integrated English use.
assessment.instructions: Complete all sections carefully. Listening passages may be played a maximum of two times. Review your answers before submitting.

questions.prompt: By the time I arrived, they ___ the meeting.
questions.explanation: Past perfect shows the earlier past action.

questions.prompt: I've ___ on this report all morning, but I've only finished two sections.
questions.explanation: The continuous form emphasizes ongoing duration.

questions.prompt: By next Friday, we ___ the migration.
questions.explanation: Future perfect expresses completion before a future deadline.

questions.prompt: If she ___ earlier, she would have caught the train.
questions.explanation: Third conditional uses past perfect in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: If I'd accepted the offer, I ___ abroad now.
questions.option_c: would have lived only in the past
questions.explanation: Past cause with present result.

questions.prompt: The office is empty. Everyone ___ home.
questions.explanation: Past deduction uses must have + participle.

questions.prompt: The system ___ at the moment.
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive is required.

questions.prompt: Report: 'Where did you park?'
questions.option_a: She asked where I had parked.
questions.option_b: She asked where did I park.
questions.option_c: She asked me where did I parked.
questions.explanation: Reported questions use statement order and can backshift.

questions.prompt: My manager, ___ joined last year, has been promoted.
questions.explanation: Who is used in a non-defining clause about a person.

questions.prompt: I remember ___ that restaurant when I was a child.
questions.explanation: Remember doing refers to a memory.

questions.prompt: ___ the delay, we completed the work on time.
questions.explanation: Despite is followed by a noun phrase.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct generalization.
questions.explanation: Zero article is natural for the general uncountable noun.

questions.prompt: What does 'look into the problem' mean?
questions.explanation: Look into means investigate.

questions.prompt: Which connector expresses contrast?
questions.explanation: Nevertheless signals contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the natural collocation.
questions.explanation: Make progress is the standard collocation.

questions.prompt: Which phrase is most appropriate in a formal request?
questions.option_a: I would appreciate it if you could...
questions.explanation: This is appropriately formal.

questions.prompt: Which form expresses strong negative deduction?
questions.explanation: Can't can express strong logical impossibility.

questions.prompt: Which relative form expresses possession?
questions.explanation: Whose indicates possession.

questions.prompt: Adjective form of 'rely':
questions.explanation: Reliable is the adjective.

questions.prompt: What does 'turn down an offer' mean?
questions.explanation: Turn down means reject.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains an error?
questions.option_a: If I'd known, I'd have called.
questions.option_b: If she had left earlier, she'd have arrived on time.
questions.option_c: If he would have studied, he would have passed.
questions.option_d: If they hadn't missed the exit, they wouldn't have been late.
questions.explanation: Use 'If he had studied'.

questions.prompt: The lights are off and nobody is answering. They ___ already.
questions.explanation: This is a strong past deduction.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct reported question.
questions.option_a: She asked where I had parked.
questions.option_b: She asked where had I parked.
questions.option_c: She asked where did I park.
questions.option_d: She asked me where I did park.
questions.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order.

questions.prompt: Choose the best connector: 'The initial cost is high; ___, the long-term savings may justify it.'
questions.explanation: Nevertheless introduces contrast.

passages.title: Rethinking Urban Workspaces
passages.instructions: Read the text and answer the four questions.
passages.content_text: Over the last few years, several companies have reduced the amount of permanent office space they use. The change has been driven partly by remote work, but cost and sustainability have also influenced the decision. Large offices that remain half empty are expensive to heat, cool, and maintain. Consequently, some organizations have moved toward smaller shared spaces that employees use only when necessary. Supporters argue that this approach reduces costs and may lower environmental impact. Nevertheless, the transition is not always simple. Employees who visit the office less frequently may find it harder to build informal relationships, and new staff may need more structured support. In addition, shared desks require careful booking systems and reliable technology. Some companies have therefore introduced 'team days' when specific groups are expected to be present. Whereas fully remote models prioritize flexibility, these hybrid approaches attempt to preserve face-to-face collaboration. Whether they succeed often depends less on the office itself than on how clearly managers define expectations and communication practices.

questions.prompt: Why have some companies reduced permanent office space?
questions.option_b: Remote work, cost, and sustainability factors
questions.explanation: The text gives several contributing reasons.

questions.prompt: What problem may new staff experience?
questions.option_b: Less informal support and relationship building
questions.explanation: The text notes that new staff may need structured support.

questions.prompt: What does 'Nevertheless' introduce?
questions.option_b: An example of a team day
questions.explanation: It contrasts benefits with implementation challenges.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest is especially important for success?
questions.explanation: The final sentence emphasizes management and communication.

passages.title: A Data Incident
passages.instructions: Read the text and answer the four questions.
passages.content_text: A regional company recently discovered that several confidential files had been copied from an internal server. At first, managers assumed that an external attacker must have gained access. However, the security team found no evidence that the network had been broken into. They then considered whether an employee might have downloaded the files accidentally while preparing a large backup. System logs showed that one account had transferred an unusually large amount of data late at night. The employee who owned the account said he had been at home at the time and had not used the system. Investigators concluded that his password might have been compromised. The account was immediately disabled, and all users were required to change their passwords. The company has since introduced additional authentication controls. Although the exact method of access could not be proved with complete certainty, the evidence suggests that weak account security, rather than a direct attack on the server, was probably responsible.

questions.prompt: What did managers initially assume?
questions.option_a: An external attacker had gained access
questions.explanation: They first suspected an external attacker.

questions.prompt: What did investigators think might have happened to the employee's account?
questions.explanation: They suspected password/account compromise.

questions.prompt: What action was taken immediately?
questions.explanation: The account was disabled.

questions.prompt: How certain is the final conclusion?
questions.explanation: The wording is cautious and evidence-based.

passages.title: Project Status Update
passages.instructions: Listen to the update. You may play the audio twice.
passages.audio_text: Here's a quick update on the migration project. By the end of today, the infrastructure team will have moved all non-critical services to the new environment. Tomorrow morning, they'll be monitoring system performance while the application team begins final testing. At this time on Thursday, we'll be reviewing the test results with the client. If everything goes according to plan, we'll have completed the full migration by Friday evening. However, we may still be making minor configuration changes over the weekend. Please avoid scheduling any major releases until Monday.

questions.prompt: What will have been moved by the end of today?
questions.explanation: Non-critical services will have been moved.

questions.prompt: What will the infrastructure team be doing tomorrow morning?
questions.explanation: They will be monitoring system performance.

questions.prompt: When is the full migration expected to be complete?
questions.explanation: Completion is expected by Friday evening.

questions.prompt: Why should major releases be avoided until Monday?
questions.explanation: Some configuration work may continue over the weekend.

passages.title: A Formal Recommendation
passages.instructions: Listen to the recommendation. You may play the audio twice.
passages.audio_text: Based on the results of the three-month pilot, I would recommend continuing the flexible scheduling policy. Attendance at team meetings has remained stable, while employee satisfaction has increased. Nevertheless, several managers reported difficulty coordinating last-minute discussions. I therefore suggest keeping two fixed office days each week and allowing teams to choose where they work on the remaining days. This approach would preserve flexibility without removing regular opportunities for face-to-face collaboration. If the policy is approved, I would also recommend reviewing it again after six months.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker recommending overall?
questions.explanation: The speaker recommends continuing the policy.

questions.prompt: What problem did some managers report?
questions.explanation: Coordination was the concern.

questions.prompt: What compromise is suggested?
questions.option_a: Two fixed office days plus flexible remaining days
questions.explanation: The proposal balances office contact and flexibility.

questions.prompt: When should the policy be reviewed again?
questions.explanation: A six-month review is recommended.
